text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Acting Finance Minister Siniora holds talks with foreign diplomats ahead of the December 16 meeting in Washington of a consultative group of nations to help finance Lebanon's postwar reconstruction.
-French President Chirac tells top Lebanese officials in telegrams that France backs Lebanon's independence and sovereignty.
-Agriculture Minister Fakhoury told delegates from 193 countries at FAO conference in Rome: "Lebanon is being invaded by toxic waste".
-Lebanon's school teachers went on a one-day strike to press the government to pay them overdue salary increases.
-Syrian Vice-President Khaddam says Syria backs a strong government in Lebanon.
-Israeli shelling damages a house in south Lebanon.
-Prosecuter-general Addoum says judicial authorities will deal firmly with the issues of corruption and toxic waste.
-A meeting of labour unionists and opposition politicians will be held today to discuss the social demands and the audiovisual media issue.

-Employees of the audovisual media decided to hold a sit-in in front of the parliament on November 19 to protest the government's decision to slash the number of private television and radio stations in Lebanon.
-Societe des Grands Hotels du Liban will list its shares on the Beirut Stock Exchange within the coming few days.
-A conference of parliamentarians from French-speaking countries will be held next week in Beirut.
